Topics · Who was Muhammad?

Where did a man with no books get the Quran?

The Quran says its Prophet recited no book before it. What can be weighed, and where did all this come from?

Part 1 of 5

﴿وَمَا كُنتَ تَتْلُوا۟ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ مِن كِتَـٰبٍ وَلَا تَخُطُّهُۥ بِيَمِينِكَ ۖ إِذًا لَّٱرْتَابَ ٱلْمُبْطِلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And you did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you inscribe one with your right hand. Then [i.e., otherwise] the falsifiers would have had [cause for] doubt.

Quran · Al-Ankabut 29:48

Start with what this book says of its own Prophet: before it he recited no book and wrote none with his hand. Then see what it adds: had it been otherwise, the doubters would have had their case. That claim could be tested the moment it was spoken, because those who heard it had known him all his life. The book rests its argument on what his neighbours could examine, and leaves it where they could reach it.

A question for you

If this claim were false, who would have been best placed to expose it?

If you sayThe people he grew up among.
ThenThen the claim was made before its ablest examiners. The Quran keeps much of what they said in reply, and the coming parts reach it.
If you sayHis opponents in his own city.
ThenThey had every reason to look, which makes what they said worth reading. The Quran records it.
If you sayA historian of our own time.
ThenA historian has more distance and less direct knowledge, and both count. You will find that voice at the end of this Step, in the strongest reply.

Part 2 of 5

﴿وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ رُوحًا مِّنْ أَمْرِنَا ۚ مَا كُنتَ تَدْرِى مَا ٱلْكِتَـٰبُ وَلَا ٱلْإِيمَـٰنُ وَلَـٰكِن جَعَلْنَـٰهُ نُورًا نَّهْدِى بِهِۦ مَن نَّشَآءُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ۚ وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِىٓ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And thus We have revealed to you an inspiration of Our command [i.e., the Qur’ān]. You did not know what is the Book or [what is] faith, but We have made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed, [O Muḥammad], you guide to a straight path -

Quran · Ash-Shura 42:52

Translation

He led them also by a straight way, that they might go to a city to live in.

Original · Hebrew

וַ֭יַּֽדְרִיכֵם בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יְשָׁרָ֑ה לָ֝לֶ֗כֶת אֶל־עִ֥יר מוֹשָֽׁב׃

the Psalms · 107:7

World English Bible

﴿نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ ٱلْقَصَصِ بِمَآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ وَإِن كُنتَ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلْغَـٰفِلِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

We relate to you, [O Muḥammad], the best of stories in what We have revealed to you of this Qur’ān although you were, before it, among the unaware.

Quran · Yusuf 12:3

Now look at what came through him: accounts of Noah, Abraham, Joseph, Moses, Mary and Jesus; laws on worship, family, trade and justice; and argument with his own city over all of it. The two verses say that before this he did not know what the Book or the faith were, and that he had been unaware. The book does not praise his reading. It credits everything to what reached him. It could have called him a genius. It calls him a Prophet who received.

A question for you

Which part of what he brought would be hardest for one person to gather alone?

If you sayThe stories of the prophets.
ThenThose stories have their own question, and it is worth walking with.
If you sayThe commands and laws.
ThenTheir heart matches what stands in the books before him, and that has its own Step.
If you sayAll of it, in one life.
ThenThen the question grows, and the next part counts the possible sources one by one.

Part 3 of 5

﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِى بَعَثَ فِى ٱلْأُمِّيِّـۧنَ رَسُولًا مِّنْهُمْ يَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَإِن كَانُوا۟ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِى ضَلَـٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

It is He who has sent among the unlettered [Arabs] a Messenger from themselves reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] and wisdom [i.e., the sunnah] - although they were before in clear error -

Quran · Al-Jumu'ah 62:2

Translation

Blessed is the man whom you discipline, Yah, and teach out of your law,

Original · Hebrew

אַשְׁרֵ֤י ׀ הַגֶּ֣בֶר אֲשֶׁר־תְּיַסְּרֶ֣נּוּ יָּ֑הּ וּֽמִתּוֹרָתְךָ֥ תְלַמְּדֶֽנּוּ׃

the Psalms · 94:12

World English Bible

Now look at the setting. The Quran describes his people as ummiyyin, which many scholars read as a people not yet given a scripture, and it says a messenger was raised among them, from themselves. Historians add a detail: no written Arabic Bible from that time is known. Jews and Christians did live in Arabia, and their teachings were heard there. So this was no empty land. It was a people with no scripture of their own, in their own tongue. Hold that beside what came through him.

A question for you

What does a people with no scripture of their own change in the question?

If you sayIt makes a written source harder to find.
ThenA written source, yes. Hearing is another matter, and the next part counts it among the sources.
If you sayStories travel by ear anyway.
ThenThat is the strongest reply, and it has a Step that sets it beside the Quran's answer.
If you sayI want to know what his people already held.
ThenAn exact question, and it has its own Step.

Part 4 of 5

﴿قُلْ مَن كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِّجِبْرِيلَ فَإِنَّهُۥ نَزَّلَهُۥ عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَهُدًى وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - it is [none but] he who has brought it [i.e., the Qur’ān] down upon your heart, [O Muḥammad], by permission of Allāh, confirming that which was before it and as guidance and good tidings for the believers."

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:97

Translation

The angel answered him, “I am Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God. I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.

Original · Ancient Greek

καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἐγώ εἰμι Γαβριὴλ ὁ παρεστηκὼς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ἀπεστάλην λαλῆσαι πρὸς σὲ καὶ εὐαγγελίσασθαί σοι ταῦτα·

the Gospel (Luke) · 1:19

World English Bible

Count the possible sources. He read it: the first verse of this Step says he recited no book. It came from his own mind: then his life among his people is the evidence, and the Quran appeals to their memory (10:16). People taught him, or he gathered it by ear: this was said in his time, and some historians propose it now; the Quran quotes the charge without a name and answers it. Or it reached him from beyond himself: the verse says it came down on his heart.

A question for you

Which source seems likeliest to you at this moment?

If you sayHe gathered it from people around him.
ThenThat is the strongest human explanation, and it deserves a fair hearing. The next Step sets it beside the Quran's own answer.
If you sayHe composed it from his own mind.
ThenThen his lifetime among them becomes the evidence to weigh.
If you sayIt reached him from beyond himself.
ThenThen the next question is what it confirmed, and whether you can see that for yourself.
If you sayI do not know yet.
ThenAn honest place to stand. The stories are a good place to keep looking.

Part 5 of 5

﴿عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنكَ لِمَ أَذِنتَ لَهُمْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكَ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا۟ وَتَعْلَمَ ٱلْكَـٰذِبِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Allāh has pardoned you, [O Muḥammad, but] why did you give them permission [to remain behind]? [You should not have] until it was evident to you who were truthful and you knew [who were] the liars.

Quran · At-Tawbah 9:43

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِىُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَآ أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكَ ۖ تَبْتَغِى مَرْضَاتَ أَزْوَٰجِكَ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O Prophet, why do you prohibit [yourself from] what Allāh has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allāh is Forgiving and Merciful.

Quran · At-Tahrim 66:1

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰٓ١ أَن جَآءَهُ ٱلْأَعْمَىٰ٢﴾

Translation of the meaning

He [i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ) ] frowned and turned away Because there came to him the blind man,[1853] [interrupting].

Translator's notes

[1853] ʿAbdullāh, the son of Umm Maktūm.

Quran · Abasa 80:1-2

Translation

“‘You shall not curse the deaf, nor put a stumbling block before the blind; but you shall fear your God. I am Yahweh.

Original · Hebrew

לֹא־תְקַלֵּ֣ל חֵרֵ֔שׁ וְלִפְנֵ֣י עִוֵּ֔ר לֹ֥א תִתֵּ֖ן מִכְשֹׁ֑ל וְיָרֵ֥אתָ מֵּאֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

the Torah (Leviticus) · 19:14

World English Bible

One more thing goes on the table. This same book addresses the Prophet and does not flatter him. God pardon you: why did you give them leave? Why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? He frowned and turned away. He recited these words to those around him, and they were kept. Now gather it: no book recited before it, a people with no scripture, no teacher the Quran names, one message with the prophets before him, and a book that addresses its bearer this way.

A question for you

Which of these strands weighs most with you?

If you sayWhat the Quran says of his learning.
ThenA Step examines that statement closely.
If you sayThat the charge, as the Quran keeps it, names no teacher.
ThenRead the charge as the Quran keeps it, and its answer.
If you sayThe one message across the prophets.
ThenThat has its own Step, with five names in one verse.
If you sayHow the book addresses him.
ThenThat question has its own Step too.

The same in the other books

Translation

Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.

Original · Hebrew

נֵר־לְרַגְלִ֥י דְבָרֶ֑ךָ וְ֝א֗וֹר לִנְתִיבָתִֽי׃

the Psalms · 119:105

World English Bible
